sources.title: Czech Foreign Ministry: Information booklet
sources.note: Printed page 8: interwar territories, Munich, German occupation and separate Slovak state, 1945 restoration, 1948 takeover.

sources.title: Czech Foreign Ministry: Welcome to the Czech Republic
sources.note: Historical overview: Velvet Revolution and peaceful division on 1 January 1993.

sources.title: Czech Parliament: Constitutional Charter of 1920
sources.note: Primary law 121/1920; section 1(1) writing sample and sections 8-10 voting rights.

sources.title: Comenius University Faculty of Medicine: Poslanie a história
sources.note: Slovak institutional history: 27 June 1919 law, Czech and Slovak instruction, professors from Prague and seven initial clinics. English version incorrectly gives July for the law, so use the Slovak witness.

sources.title: Comenius University: History of the medical physics institute
sources.note: 1923/24 first-year instruction, gymnasium premises and 1926 move to purpose-built theoretical institutes.

sources.title: City of Zlín: Baťovy internáty, 1930-1937
sources.note: Fourteen-year-old young workers, 1925 first dormitory, 1927 onward district, Gahura reinforced concrete module 6.15 by 6.15 meters and communal ground floors.

sources.title: National Technical Museum: Contact lenses
sources.note: Wichterle soft lens material and casting method; museum objects include an early 1961 machine and separately a later model of the Merkur apparatus.

sources.title: National Technical Museum: Merkur construction set exhibition
sources.note: Vancl construction toys, bolts and nuts from 1925, Christmas 1961 lens apparatus.

sources.title: National Museum: A century of tramping
sources.note: Weekend camping, Wild West inspiration, journals, music, totems and police-confiscated flags in the exhibition.

sources.title: National Museum: History of the House of Fashion
sources.note: 1956 Prague store and captioned checked cotton dress, Módní závody Praha, 1956-1960. Broad claims that ideology ceased to affect clothing are not adopted.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia, 1968
sources.note: Dubček reforms, Prague Spring and August Warsaw Pact invasion.

sources.title: Czech Parliament: Constitution of the Czech Republic
sources.note: Enacted constitution of 16 December 1992, article 1(1); effective 1 January 1993.

sources.title: ELI Beamlines: European-American partnership in laser technologies
sources.note: HAPLS developed with Lawrence Livermore 2013-2017, integrated at ELI in 2018; planned upgrades are not reported as achieved.

sources.title: ELI Beamlines: L3-HAPLS laser
sources.note: International engineering, compressor, diagnostics, controls and helium-cooled amplifiers; rated parameters not equated with routine operation.

sources.title: UNESCO: Puppetry in Slovakia and Czechia
sources.note: 2016 inscription; wooden puppets, traveling families, local language, making and performing skills. Shared source across Czech and Slovak cards.

sources.title: UNESCO: Resist block printing and indigo dyeing in Europe
sources.note: Resist paste, indigo, carved blocks, family workshops and nineteenth-century recipe notebooks. Multinational practice.

sources.title: UNESCO: Christmas decorations from blown glass beads
sources.note: 2020 inscription; molded glass tubes, silvering, coloring and wire assembly; Kulhavý workshop survived economic transformation.

sources.title: UNESCO: Žatec and the Landscape of Saaz Hops
sources.note: 2023 inscription; fields, drying barns, kilns, warehouses and certification, continuing use and reuse.

sources.title: Prague water utility: History and construction of the wastewater treatment plant
sources.note: 2002 flood and new line designed to resist floodwater, raised terrain and publicly accessible park.

sources.title: Czech government: Czech educational system
sources.note: Current government description of nine-year compulsory schooling, checked September 2026.

sources.title: Slovak Foreign Ministry: Mission Slovakia
sources.note: Independent republic founded at midnight on 1 January 1993 after division of federal Czechoslovakia.

sources.title: Slovak Academy of Sciences: Space Research in Slovakia 2018-2019
sources.note: Printed page 10, skCUBE: 23 June 2017 launch, universities, more than sixty volunteers, partial failure, 569 days and end of mission.

sources.title: International Court of Justice: Gabčíkovo-Nagymaros Project
sources.note: Overview: 1977 treaty, Slovakia as successor, 1997 site visit and judgment. Do not confuse permission to construct with lawful operation of the provisional solution.

sources.title: Danubiana museum: History
sources.note: Opening 9 September 2000, Meulensteen and Polakovič, Čunovo peninsula and international exhibitions.

sources.title: Danubiana museum: History and collections
sources.note: Public nonprofit structure in 2012 and collections of international paintings, contemporary Slovak art and outdoor sculpture.

sources.title: Slovak Intangible Cultural Heritage Centre: Cultural heritage of Slovakia
sources.note: Printed page 11: fujara, long pipe with three finger holes, central Slovak shepherd tradition, individual decoration.

sources.title: Slovakia Travel: Tinkering
sources.note: National tourism account of wire and tin repair craft, traveling tinkers and present Považské Museum displays at Budatín.

sources.title: Slovak Ministry of Education: System of schools and school facilities
sources.note: Current description, compulsory attendance ten years and until the school year in which a pupil reaches sixteen; checked September 2026.

sources.title: European Commission: Slovakia and the euro
sources.note: EU membership 2004, euro adoption 1 January 2009, conversion 30.1260 koruna per euro and dual circulation through 16 January.

sources.title: Slovak Parliament: Constitution, consolidated 2019
sources.note: Article 1(1), Slovak wording in official consolidated witness dated 22 August 2019; constitution originally adopted in 1992.

sources.title: Slovenian Government: Independence and Unity Day
sources.note: December 1990 plebiscite and confirmation of independence on 25 June 1991.

sources.title: Slovenia: Fourth national report, state organization
sources.note: Section 2.1: independence 25 June 1991, constitution 23 December 1991, EU membership 1 May 2004.

sources.title: City Museum of Ljubljana: Ljubljana during the war for Slovenia in 1991
sources.note: Photographic exhibition: air-raid sirens, shopping, parents appealing for sons, press conferences and ordinary people in the 1991 war.

sources.title: UNESCO: Beekeeping in Slovenia, a way of life
sources.note: 2022 nomination description: family apiaries, Carniolan bees, painted panels, intergenerational knowledge. No medical efficacy claims adopted.

sources.title: UNESCO: Bobbin lacemaking in Slovenia
sources.note: 2018 description: bobbins, pinned patterns and cylindrical pillows, household textiles, family and community transmission.

sources.title: Slovenian Government: Launch of NEMO-HD and TRISAT
sources.note: 3 September 2020 launch; NEMO-HD 65 kg, interactive video and multispectral sensing; TRISAT 5 kg, miniature electronics and optical sensor. Describes intended functions, not proof of all outcomes.

sources.title: City of Ljubljana: Environment in the City of Ljubljana 2017
sources.note: Reuse Centre section: opened 2013, repair and reuse, employment opportunities, shoe cupboard made from a gaming machine.

sources.title: RCERO Ljubljana: Regional waste management centre
sources.note: Operator description: mechanical and biological treatment facilities and treatment of landfill leachate, operation from late 2015.

sources.title: Slovenian Government: About basic school
sources.note: Current nine-year basic education from age six, after-school program for years 1-5; checked September 2026.

sources.title: UNESCO: Škofja Loka Passion Play
sources.note: 2016 description, 900 performers and 400 volunteers, older local language, twenty street scenes and community preparation.

sources.title: Slovenian Government: Slovenia and the 2030 Agenda
sources.note: Right to Water in the Constitution section, amendment adopted 2016. Legal principle, not a claim of flawless delivery.

sources.title: Slovenian legal information system: Constitution, consolidated text 5
sources.note: Article 1, official consolidated text including amendments through 2004; constitution enacted 23 December 1991.

sources.title: Miroslav Krleža Institute of Lexicography: Development of the state
sources.note: Royal succession, Zvonimir and papacy, Coloman 1102, later Croatian institutions, and modern independence. Pacta conventa survives as a later text, not an authenticated 1102 original.

sources.title: Croatian Technical Encyclopedia: Kondura
sources.note: Nin finds dated eleventh-twelfth centuries, remains 7 and 8 meters long, oars and square sails, conservation and modern replica.

sources.title: Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts: Baška tablet
sources.note: Circa 1100, St Lucy at Jurandvor, dimensions and thirteen Glagolitic lines; Branko Fučić Latin transcription and English translation.

sources.title: Benedictines of Zadar: Čika and Vekenega
sources.note: Community history of foundation in 1066, Čika and daughters, Vekenega abbacy 1095-1111; surviving cartulary entries 1066-1236 in several scripts. Legendary details omitted.

sources.title: Croatian Ministry of Culture: Radovan portal
sources.note: Portal of St Lawrence, Trogir: inscribed date 1240, Radovan and Bishop Treguan.

sources.title: Vladimir Peter Goss, Matica hrvatska: Per Raduanum
sources.note: Art historian, Vijenac 809, 13 March 2025: title quotes Latin signature; opening describes 1240 inscription, central Nativity and later additions.

sources.title: Zagreb City Museum: Golden Bull 1242-1992
sources.note: 16 November 1242 charter for Gradec, royal seal, local administration, court, taxes, markets and bounds.

sources.title: Zagreb City Museum: Construction of the cathedral
sources.note: Twelfth-century three-aisled Romanesque cathedral, destruction in 1242 and subsequent Gothic rebuilding.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Zagreb: Branimirova godina 2019
sources.note: Printed pages 64-65: earrings with hollow beads, including Biskupija near Knin; tenth-eleventh-century forms and Byzantine cultural connections.

sources.title: United Nations: UNTAES mission overview
sources.note: Mandate completed 15 January 1998, peaceful reintegration of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Sirmium.

sources.title: United Nations: UNTAES background
sources.note: Council requirements concerning return, pensions, welfare, policing, tolerance and implementation of amnesty.

sources.title: Museum of Apoxyomenos: Exhibition and conservation
sources.note: Six years of conservation; second-first century BCE bronze, interior mouse nest, laurel leaves and fruit remains. Ancient object, modern recovery and research.

sources.title: Croatian Museum Documentation Centre: Museum of Apoxyomenos
sources.note: Museum profile: underwater discovery 1996, recovery 27 April 1999, museum opened 2016. Calendar query parameters do not date the object or museum.

sources.title: UNESCO: Wooden toys in Hrvatsko Zagorje
sources.note: 2009 description, local woods, family carving and painting, changing toy forms and musical instruments.

sources.title: UNESCO: Gingerbread craft from Northern Croatia, nomination
sources.note: 2010 nomination section 2: family craft, heart ornaments with mirrors and messages, wood and metal molds, connections with candle and honey-drink production.

sources.title: European Commission in Croatia: Pelješac Bridge
sources.note: Opening 26 July 2022, 2.4 km bridge, four traffic lanes and 55-meter clearance.

sources.title: World Bank and Croatian Government: Earthquake rapid damage and needs assessment 2020
sources.note: Education section: 22 March 2020 earthquake, 513 education facilities damaged, schools closed for COVID-19, estimated 6,200 pupils needing relocation.

sources.title: European Union: Croatia country profile
sources.note: EU membership 2013, euro adoption 1 January 2023; continuing state profile.

sources.title: Croatian Government: Primary education
sources.note: Compulsory free primary schooling, at least eight years; parallel music and dance education. Checked September 2026.

sources.title: Croatian Constitutional Court: Constitution, consolidated text
sources.note: Article 1, exact Croatian word order; editorial consolidation dated 15 January 2014 of constitution enacted 22 December 1990.

sources.title: Croatian Parliament: 25 June, Independence Day
sources.note: Declaration 25 June 1991, implementation moratorium and severance of remaining ties 8 October 1991.

sources.title: Museum of Yugoslavia: Historical timeline
sources.note: Timeline: 1918 kingdom, 1929 name and dictatorship, 1945 republic, 1948 split and repression, 1950 workers management, 1961 Non-Aligned summit, 1965 reform and migration, 1992 FRY.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Breakup of Yugoslavia
sources.note: Overview of wartime partition and socialist federation, 1991-1992 dissolution and wars. Avoid its imprecise May 1992 date for Bosnian independence.

sources.title: Archives of Yugoslavia: Constitutive acts of Yugoslavia
sources.note: 1946 federation and 1953 constitutional law, workers and producers self-management.

sources.title: Archives of Yugoslavia: Constitution of 1946
sources.note: PDF page index 1, printed page 5, article 1. Archival edition/transcription in Serbian Cyrillic, not a facsimile of the original gazette.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum: Jasenovac
sources.note: Axis partition, Ustaša regime and concentration camp system; victims included Serbs, Jews, Roma and political opponents. No disputed numerical claims included.

sources.title: Museum of Modern Art: Toward a Concrete Utopia, section texts
sources.note: Housing section: rapid urbanization, prefabrication, flexible layouts, multifunctional spaces and balconies; architectural competitions and publications.

sources.title: MoMA Post: Curating the Yugoslav identity, reconstruction of Skopje
sources.note: 1963 earthquake, international reconstruction, Kenzo Tange and local planning context.

sources.title: Museum of Architecture and Design: ETA 80 telephone
sources.note: Cvetka Požar, 2014 collection note: Davorin Savnik, Iskra, 1979, flat clean form; exhibited but never awarded at BIO.

sources.title: Rex Kralj: Rex Lounge Chair
sources.note: Manufacturer heritage record: Niko Kralj, folding lounge version 1956, bent and cut plywood. Do not confuse with earlier 1952 development or 1953 stacking chair.

sources.title: Museum of Yugoslavia: Hedgehog’s House, inventing a better world
sources.note: Printed page 128, figure 2: Branko Ćopić first edition Ježeva kuća, 1949, Aljoša Josić illustrations, 5,000 copies, 1951 Italian translation. No verse reproduced.

sources.title: Museum of Yugoslavia: Selection of ten objects, Prvoslav Vučković
sources.note: 11 April 2025, indexed museum text describing youth work actions, inter-brigade labor and cultural/sports competitions, songs and greetings. Direct fetch sometimes challenge-protected.

sources.title: Hellenic Parliament: Constitutional history
sources.note: Greek-language institutional history: 1924 republic, Metaxas dictatorship, 1967-1974 junta and democratic restoration; referendum December 1974. English version has a 1922 typo for the March 1924 declaration; Greek original used.

sources.title: Hellenic Parliament television: The interwar republic, 1924-1935
sources.note: Institutional program description: abolition of monarchy in 1924, restoration in 1935.

sources.title: Greek Foreign Ministry Diplomatic and Historical Archives: International treaties and protocols
sources.note: London Protocol of 3 February 1830, first formal international act recognizing Greece as an entirely independent state.

sources.title: Panathenaic Stadium: Modern stadium
sources.note: Official stadium history of rebuilding for the 1896 modern Olympic Games.

sources.title: Benaki Museum: On Relics, Asia Minor
sources.note: 2022 exhibition: 1922-1924 refugees in Drama, temporary shelter in churches, mosques and houses, Santirvan mosque, rescued objects.

sources.title: EYDAP: Attica waters
sources.note: Utility historical account: population and supply pressures after 1922, Marathon dam, tunnel and new water network replacing older system.

sources.title: EYDAP: Annual report 2017, Water Museum
sources.note: Water Museum section: Marathon dam construction October 1926-October 1929; workers stone houses from 1926, tools and construction film.

sources.title: Elliniko Metro: Archaeological excavations
sources.note: Company overview of archaeological work associated with Athens metro construction, approximately 79,000 square meters excavated and 50,000 finds.

sources.title: Elliniko Metro: Archaeology, excavation areas
sources.note: Syntagma, Keramikos, Monastiraki and Akropoli; ancient water structures, wells, conduits and reservoirs uncovered at depth.

sources.title: UNESCO: Mastic know-how on Chios, 2012 decision
sources.note: Detailed description of resin production and family/community roles. Nomination was referred in 2012, not inscribed then; no inscription claim made here.

sources.title: Centre for the Greek Language: Historical dictionary and modern Greek
sources.note: Conference paper pages 209-221; demotic established in education 1976 and administration 1977.

sources.title: European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies: Greece health system review 2010
sources.note: Overview: ESY founded 1983, mixture of public and private provision and uneven access; historical claims only, not current medical guidance.

sources.title: Mediterranean Diet emblematic communities network: At the heart of the Mediterranean table
sources.note: 2025 first-person account by chef Panagiotis at Artaki restaurant in Koroni: seasonal ingredients, vegetable leftovers in pies and fish bones for stock. Specific testimony, not all Greek households.

sources.title: Hellenic Parliament: Constitution, article 1
sources.note: Article 1(3), modern Greek demotic wording introduced in 1986, in official consolidated constitution through 2019. Not presented as unchanged wording of the 1975 first edition.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Decoded Czechoslovak geometry includes interwar Carpathian Ruthenia, later excluded. The imported 1938 shape must not imply continuous domestic state control through the 1939-1945 rupture. Formal dissolution was 31 December 1992, despite imported transition in 1994. No grouping with modern Czechia.
Separate modern states. Slovakia begins politically in 1993 and Slovenia in 1991, although both imported labels begin in 1994. Neither is grouped with earlier kingdoms or the wartime Slovak state.

Do not group. Medieval Croatia has repeated 1000/1100/1200 geometry with bbox approximately 14.355,43.390,16.864,45.865; modern imported record begins 1994. Medieval cultural examples include connected coastal towns and neighboring Croatian-Slavonian institutions beyond the schematic polygon. The modern 1994 polygon does not document actual control over all territory that year. Eastern peaceful reintegration completed January 1998. No geometry changes made.

Imported 1920-1994 coverage spans Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, kingdom named Yugoslavia from 1929, wartime rupture, and socialist federation. Do not equate 1992 Serbia-Montenegro FRY with the six-republic SFRY. 1945 and 1960 geometry differ in western/Istrian coverage. Dissolution is a 1991-1992 process, not a 1994 event.

Imported modern Greece starts 1878, although political independence predates this. Decoded 1878/1880 geometry extends implausibly north to about 42.857N. The 1930 geometry prematurely includes Dodecanese islands including Karpathos, Tilos, Symi and Leros, then under Italy. Later 1945/1960/1994/2000/2010 sampled geometries extend only to about 26.646E and omit Dodecanese territory that joined Greece in 1947. These are upstream geometry defects; narrative acceptance does not validate the borders. No geometry edits performed.
